name: Rasmus Busk
profile: Danish co-founder of Copenhagen card-payments company Flatpay (launched 2022) alongside CEO Sander Janca-Jensen, Peter Lüth and Rasmus Hellmund Carlsen. He leads Flatpay's international expansion as it rolls out flat-fee payment terminals for small merchants across Europe; a €145M round valued the company at €1.5B.
interesting_fact: Flatpay was reported as the fastest Danish company ever to reach unicorn status; the four co-founders had previously co-founded startups together.
deep_cut_fact: Before Flatpay he and Sander Janca-Jensen worked in field sales at home-security company Verisure, where they scaled a sales team of 400 — the playbook behind Flatpay's direct field-sales model.

public_contacts.value: christian.gronning@flatpay.dk (Christian Grønning, Global Head of Communications)

notes: Low public profile; some databases misspell him 'Rasmus Bush'. Route via Flatpay comms.

name: Jason Guss
current_role: CEO & Co-founder, Octane (Octane Lending, Inc.), New York
profile: Yale graduate and former Capital One corporate-strategy consultant who co-founded Octane in New York in 2014. Octane provides instant financing (via its lender Roadrunner Financial) for powersports, RV, marine and outdoor power equipment purchases; it raised a $100M Series F led by Valar Ventures in Dec 2025, reportedly at a ~$1.3B valuation.
interesting_fact: Octane was GAAP-profitable in 2021; Guss's two rules for running a lender: 'don't run out of money and don't over lever the business.'
deep_cut_fact: Besides running Octane he has made angel investments in nearly 30 fintech startups.
notes: Valuation ~$1.3B per third-party reports of the Series F; Octane's own release does not state valuation. Has appeared on fintech podcasts (Fintech Leaders) — receptive to podcast format.

name: Radu Banabic
current_role: Co-founder & VP of Engineering, Cyberhaven (per EPFL DSLAB alumni listing)
profile: Romanian computer scientist (BSc Technical University of Cluj-Napoca; EPFL PhD 2015 under George Candea) who co-founded data-security company Cyberhaven in 2016 with Candea and fellow lab members. Cyberhaven, now led by CEO Howard Ting, sells data-lineage-based data loss prevention and was valued at $1B+.
interesting_fact: His EPFL PhD thesis, 'Techniques for Identifying Elusive Corner-Case Bugs in Systems Software', included Achilles, a tool that hunts for 'Trojan messages' in distributed systems.
deep_cut_fact: As an undergraduate research assistant in Cluj he built a model for detecting automobile window pillars in live images for a project with Volkswagen AG, and graduated with a 9.92/10 GPA; he also interned at IBM Research Zurich (2012) on a distributed storage algorithm.
notes: Very low public profile engineer. Current title from EPFL lab alumni page; not confirmed on Cyberhaven's site. Old EPFL email on his CV is likely inactive — not listed.
